claims.text: The examined particles are initially solid Fe-Ni-Cr-Co-Cu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Premelting and melting behavior is governed by an interplay between chemical complexity and nanoscale phase-transition behavior.
In-situ X-ray diffraction, transmission electron microscopy, or differential scanning calorimetry can reveal the governing thermal response.
Chemical complexity influences the thermal response of the nanoparticles.
Nanoscale phase-transition behavior influences the thermal response of the nanoparticles.
The proposed interplay leads to varied nanoparticle configurations.
The proposed interplay leads to phase transitions.
The Fe-Ni-Cr-Co-Cu nanoparticles will have altered melting points relative to single-metal or bimetallic particles.
The Fe-Ni-Cr-Co-Cu nanoparticles will exhibit different phase-transition behavior from single-metal or bimetallic particles.
The Fe-Ni-Cr-Co-Cu nanoparticles will exhibit different structural changes from single-metal or bimetallic particles.
The hypothesis is restricted to the premelting and melting regime.
Thermal behavior identical to that of single-metal or bimetallic particles would falsify the hypothesis.
Finding no significant influence of chemical complexity or nanoscale phase-transition behavior on thermal response would falsify the hypothesis.
